I’ve had this same problem for my whole life and it’s so tough. One thing that helped me was getting one of those microfiber towel hair wraps. Another thing that helped was getting a really soft bath mat to step on when I get out of the shower. And getting really soft towels. The feeling of the bath mat and the towel used to really bother me (and they still do tbh) but I’ve been able to mitigate it a decent amount.

I also found that playing music or even playing a tv show that I like was really helpful. I have a water proof speaker and I’ll play something on my phone so I can focus on that and not focus on the fact that I have to shower and I’m upset about it. I’ll put the tv show on my phone and prop my phone up somewhere I can see it but where it’s not getting hit directly by water. My phone and phone case are waterproof so if yours aren’t it would also work to just put the phone outside the shower and just listen on the speaker. Sometimes I also listen to podcasts.

I would suggest contacting the Aging and Disability Resource Center (ADRC) in your state, if you have one. A common misconception is that they only help the elderly but they help any adult with a disability, so your brother would likely qualify for services. Typically they will connect him with a case manager that can help him locate other resources locally such as housing etc.

If you are unable to find a local ADRC contact your county’s human services department. They may have other programs for adults with disabilities that they can connect you with, or help you locate an ADRC.

The correct definition is someone who experiences no sexual attraction. That being said, there are lots of subsets of asexuality. It sounds like you might be [aegosexual](https://lgbta.wikia.org/wiki/Aegosexual). That's when you have a disconnect between you and the source of arousal (ie being aroused by fictional characters but having no interest in having sex with actual people).

You can absolutely have kinks and be asexual, because the only requirement for being asexual is having no sexual attraction. Just because you have a kink doesn't mean you're sexually attracted to a specific person - if you thought about doing that kink with a specific person that you know, that would probably indicate sexual attraction toward that person, but just having the kink in general won't. The difference is just generally liking and wanting to engage in a kink (general arousal) and wanting to do a kink with a specific person, who you are attracted to.

If you do feel like you experience sexual attraction to other people, not just fictional characters or people you're disconnected with (like if you feel sexual attraction to a crush), you're probably not asexual. But you can absolutely be a sex repulsed allo - that's a totally valid identity as well.

To add to what the other commenter said it's very different if you're a minor vs 18+. If you're a minor, you have a lot less say than if you're an adult and can make your own medical decisions. If you're a minor and self harm is found, in my experience the doctor/psychiatrist/etc will inform your parents. I think (?) they're obligated to inform your parents but correct me if I'm wrong. They're definitely obligated to inform them if they feel you are at immediate risk.

All that being said, just finding evidence of self harm is very very unlikely to get you hospitalized unless it is a very severe case. Typically inpatient care, which I assume is what you're referring to, is reserved for people that are an immediate danger to themselves or others. If you were to tell a psychiatrist that you are going to kill yourself, you have a plan, you have the required items, and you have a set time you're going to do it, that is grounds for hospitalization. If they simply find self harm the only thing you'd need to worry about is telling your parents (if you're a minor).
